finding.get_task: GetTaskRequest is Request<GetTaskMethod, GetTaskParams>. GetTaskParams publicly contains meta: Option<RequestMetaObject> serialized as _meta and implements RequestParamsMeta::meta_mut().
finding.update_task: UpdateTaskRequest is Request<UpdateTaskMethod, UpdateTaskParams>. UpdateTaskParams publicly contains meta: Option<RequestMetaObject> serialized as _meta and implements RequestParamsMeta::meta_mut().
finding.cancel_task: CancelTaskRequest is Request<CancelTaskMethod, CancelTaskParams>. CancelTaskParams publicly contains meta: Option<RequestMetaObject> serialized as _meta and implements RequestParamsMeta::meta_mut().
finding.wrapper: Generic Request<M,P>::new(params) preserves the supplied params and initializes only wrapper Extensions to default; Request itself exposes extensions_mut(), but the params-only convenience helpers do not accept a prebuilt wrapper.
finding.contract: The task client convenience signatures have no separate metadata argument, but task protocol _meta is still caller-reachable: set params.meta (directly or through RequestParamsMeta::meta_mut) before calling get_task/update_task/cancel_task, and XRequest::new(params) carries that _meta-bearing params object into the typed request. Wrapper Extensions remain a distinct seam and are not caller-supplied through those convenience helpers.
finding.scope_correction: Revision 111's narrow statement about no explicit metadata parameter on the helper signatures remains true; it must not be generalized into 'task request _meta is inaccessible'.
